children.text: Maturity labels
Every Labs asset carries a maturity label, shown above the fold, that says what exists:
Research: exploration or analysis; not a client product.
Concept: a defined idea with limited implementation evidence.
Prototype: a working proof designed to test feasibility.
Accelerator: a reusable internal or client delivery component.
Beta / Pilot: limited use with explicit constraints.
Production product: only when a separately supported commercial product genuinely exists.
Each asset states what it is, what it is not and its known limitations.

heading: Strategy and engineering, connected by responsibility for the outcome.
intro: Vitalos is a technology consulting, engineering and digital transformation company with AI at the centre.

children.text: Why Vitalos exists

Technology has become inseparable from how organisations operate, serve customers and compete. AI accelerates that shift, but the hard part is not choosing a model or buying another tool. It is redesigning work, modernising systems, connecting data, making good engineering decisions and carrying change safely into production. Vitalos exists for that gap between ambition and execution.
From strategy to production

We work with organisations to understand what needs to change, decide where technology and AI create real value, engineer the products and platforms required, and keep improving them once they are live. That is why Vitalos is neither a strategy-only consultancy nor a build-to-spec agency.
Five practices, one firm

Consulting, Engineering, AI & Data, Experience and Managed Services share one delivery lifecycle, one accountability model and one quality philosophy. One engagement never feels like five departments.
Two ways to start
Clients can start with consulting or come directly for engineering. Discovery is used when it reduces real uncertainty or risk, not by default.
Operating principles
Senior involvement: you have access to people who can understand the problem and make decisions about it.
Evidence before claims: we prefer a verifiable fact to an adjective.
Production quality: security, reliability, maintainability and operational readiness are part of delivery.
Responsible AI: AI is used where it creates measurable value and can be governed.
Commercially sensible: scope, assumptions, responsibilities, risks and expected outcomes are explicit.
UK first, international by design

The United Kingdom is Vitalos's launch market and commercial base. The company's services, delivery standards and operating practices are designed to support international work as it grows, without pretending that geographic scale already exists.

heading: Disciplined delivery without unnecessary bureaucracy.
intro: You can start with consulting or come directly for engineering. Discovery is required when risk or uncertainty makes it necessary, and every engagement follows one delivery lifecycle with quality gates that are not waived to protect a date.

children.text: Two ways to start

Consulting-led: when you know there is a problem but not yet the right solution, discovery and assessment create the evidence and the roadmap. Engineering-led: when the objective, requirements and constraints are clear, we confirm the technical approach and build.
One accountable Engagement Lead

Every engagement has one named Vitalos Engagement Lead, accountable for the relationship, the outcome, delivery and commercial health, risk, quality and truthful reporting. You never have to coordinate separate Vitalos practices.
Quality gates

Before production or acceptance, work passes gates for architecture, security, privacy and data, functional quality, performance, accessibility, resilience and recovery, operational readiness, documentation and client acceptance, plus AI evaluation where AI is involved. A gate that does not apply is recorded as not applicable, with the reason.
Contractors under Vitalos standards

Contractors and specialist partners may extend capacity and capability, but you contract with Vitalos and Vitalos stays accountable. They follow Vitalos security, delivery, documentation and quality standards, get least-privilege access that is removed promptly, and critical knowledge never stays with one contractor. Where we partner for a capability, you know the responsibility model.
What clients can expect

Organised without bureaucracy, technically serious without being inaccessible, commercially disciplined without being adversarial, and fast without being reckless. Status reports say what is true: health with a reason, outcomes since the last report, decisions needed, top risks and owners, and the scope position. Changes to scope are handled openly, never absorbed silently.
Qualify

Should Vitalos pursue this work? We look at the business problem and the cost of doing nothing, the sponsor and decision-makers, urgency, budget, technical complexity and risk, and decide to pursue, clarify or decline.
Discover

What is actually happening and why? We gather evidence on the problem, users and processes, systems and data, risks and success measures, so the problem is understood before large commitments are made.
Define
What exactly should be done? Scope, target outcomes, architecture direction, roadmap, backlog and how acceptance will work, specific enough that both sides know what is included and excluded.
Design
How will the solution work? Service and interface design alongside technical, integration, data and security design, with material choices recorded as decision records.
Engineer

Can we build it safely and incrementally? Working increments through version control, peer review, automated checks and controlled environments. Contractors and partners work to the same Vitalos standards.
Validate

Is it fit for release and use? Functional, security, performance, accessibility, data, integration and operational-readiness checks, AI evaluation where relevant, and acceptance by a named client owner.
Release
Can we move to production safely? Deployment, migration, runbooks, monitoring, a rollback plan and training. A deadline is never approval to skip review, validation or rollback planning.
Operate
Can the live service meet its commitments? Monitoring, incident response, support, maintenance and service reporting, with ownership made explicit through a service transition.
Improve
What should change next? We compare the live system with its intended outcomes, incidents, cost, user friction and technical debt, and agree the next roadmap.

title: Vitalos Consulting
summary: Clarity, transformation choices, roadmaps and architecture before expensive execution.
proposition: Consulting helps you decide what should change, why it matters, what the target state should be and how technology, data and AI should enable it. Every engagement ends with a clear next step, in order, with its dependencies and a way to measure success.
problems: Parts of the business need modernising, but there is no coherent plan.
Nobody can say with confidence what is wrong, risky or holding the platform back.
Leadership is unsure whether the organisation, its data and its controls are ready for AI.
Technology investment over the next one to three years needs a sequenced, defensible roadmap.
Architecture or integration decisions are unresolved and implementation is about to start.
Requirements are contested, incomplete or likely to change materially.

children.text: Decisions, not slideware

Consulting must produce decisions and implementable direction. Every advisory engagement should answer what you should do next, why, in what order, with what dependencies, and how success will be measured.
Discovery when it reduces risk

Discovery exists to reduce uncertainty, not to create billable steps. It is the right start when the problem is unclear, several departments or systems are affected, legacy behaviour is poorly understood, data or AI readiness is unknown, or the investment is large enough that you need evidence before committing. A clear, low-risk build can go straight to Engineering.
How Consulting works with the other practices

Consulting is often the front door to larger programmes. Its roadmaps and architecture are written to be delivered by Engineering, AI & Data, Experience and Managed Services, so advice stays connected to what can actually be built and operated.
AI appears in Consulting as strategy, opportunity identification, operating model, governance, adoption and the business case.
Where an assessment finds that Vitalos should not implement the solution, we say so.

title: Vitalos Engineering
summary: Serious production software, modernisation, platforms, integration and reliability.
proposition: Engineering designs, builds, integrates, modernises and improves production software and platforms. You can come to us directly with a clear need, or continue from discovery, with architecture, testing, security, documentation and operational handover built into the work.
problems: A new product, portal, workflow platform or application is needed.
Ageing software holds the organisation back and is hard to change.
Platforms, services and data flows are disconnected, so people re-key information and hand work over by hand.
Infrastructure, deployments and observability make releases slow or risky.
A product is slow, unstable, unfinished or poorly engineered.
Defects and operational risk undermine confidence in every release.

children.text: Built for production

Fast must never mean careless, and enterprise must never mean unnecessarily complicated. Vitalos Engineering aims to be known for strong architecture, pragmatic implementation, production readiness, documentation, testing, security awareness and operational handover.
How we engineer

Work moves through version control, peer review, automated checks and controlled environments, so evidence builds up continuously instead of risk accumulating until the end. An increment is done when:
its acceptance criteria are met and the relevant tests pass;
it has been peer reviewed and its security and privacy requirements are satisfied;
observability covers material production paths;
operational and documentation changes are complete, with migrations and rollback considered where relevant;
no critical defect or unowned material risk remains.
Direct engineering, with judgement

Clients may come directly for engineering when the objective, requirements, constraints, decision-makers and dependencies are clear enough. We do not invent a discovery phase, but we stop and recommend one when the risk of building the wrong thing becomes material.
How Engineering works with the other practices

Engineering takes work forward from Consulting, AI & Data and Experience, and hands live systems to Managed Services through a formal transition. AI appears here as AI-enabled products, agents, integrations, inference services and secure application architecture.

seo.title: Vitalos Engineering
seo.description: Production software, application modernisation, platforms, integration, cloud and reliability engineering.

title: Vitalos AI & Data
summary: AI and data from opportunity and foundations through production and managed operation.
proposition: We help organisations identify valuable AI opportunities, build the data foundations, prototype quickly, engineer production systems and operate them responsibly. AI is used where it creates a measurable business or user outcome and can be governed.
problems: Leadership wants measurable AI value but has no safe, prioritised route from experimentation to production.
AI pilots are scattered and few have made it into production.
Data sits across several systems and is too fragmented or low-confidence to support decisions or AI.
Reporting and management information cannot be trusted.
Governance, privacy, security and human oversight of AI use are unclear.
capabilities: Data engineering, data platforms and data quality

children.text: From opportunity to production

AI follows one signature journey: AI Opportunity Assessment, then a Prototype, then Production, then Managed AI. Each stage ends with a decision: is there a use case worth testing, did the evidence justify production investment, is the system ready for controlled live use, and is it still delivering value safely.
How we approach AI
No AI for AI's sake: every use case needs a business or user outcome.
Prototype evidence does not automatically mean production readiness.
Data readiness, security, privacy and human oversight are made explicit.
Bounded, measurable workflows come before broad autonomous systems.
Evaluation criteria are defined before production launch.
Operational cost, reliability and vendor dependence are understood up front.
We stay pragmatic about technology and vendors rather than tying the work to one model provider.
Data foundations

Useful analytics and AI depend on data that is connected, cleaned, modelled and governed. Data work covers source ownership and lineage, quality expectations, schema and contract management, access control, retention and deletion rules, monitoring for pipeline failure and freshness, and documented definitions for the metrics that matter.
AI across every practice

AI & Data is a specialist practice and a horizontal capability. Consulting shapes AI strategy and governance, Engineering builds AI into products and integrations, Experience designs conversational interfaces, intelligent search and human-centred AI, and Managed Services monitors, evaluates and improves live AI.

title: Vitalos Experience
summary: Human-centred products, services, commerce and accessible digital experiences.
proposition: Experience shapes how customers, employees and partners use digital services. It connects user needs, service design, product strategy and engineering so that technology is useful, understandable and adopted, and designs can be delivered within real constraints.
problems: A new product needs defining before major engineering investment.
Usability, accessibility or conversion friction is losing customers or slowing service.
Customer self-service is fragmented and disconnected from the operational workflows behind it.
The commerce experience, and the systems and processes behind it, need modernising.
Digital products are designed and built inconsistently, without a shared component foundation.

children.text: Design that can be delivered

Experience is not a standalone graphic-design department. Its work usually connects to engineering or measurable implementation, so we avoid beautiful prototypes that cannot be delivered within your technology, operational or commercial constraints.
Accessible by default
Accessibility is part of design quality, not an after-launch audit. Interfaces are checked against the accessibility target agreed for the engagement before release.
How Experience works with the other practices

Experience leads discovery and design for new products, portals and commerce journeys, then works alongside Engineering through build and release. AI appears here as conversational interfaces, intelligent search, personalisation and human-centred AI experience design.

title: Vitalos Managed Services
summary: Reliable operation, support and continuous improvement for systems Vitalos builds or responsibly inherits.
proposition: Managed Services takes ongoing operational responsibility for live systems and keeps improving them. It covers systems Vitalos built and systems others built, but only after an assessment establishes a baseline we can responsibly support.
problems: Live systems need ongoing ownership, but there is no full internal product engineering function.
The internal team needs flexible access to multidisciplinary engineering capacity.
Deployment, monitoring and reliability take more effort than the organisation can sustain.
Products stagnate after launch instead of continuing to improve.
A system built by another supplier needs a new, accountable owner.
Production AI or data pipelines need operating, evaluating and improving under agreed controls.

children.text: Support is an operational commitment
“We will support it” is an operational commitment, not a sales phrase. Vitalos does not accept a service level for an inherited system it does not understand.
Taking over systems built by others

Before taking responsibility for a third-party or inherited system, we assess ownership and access, architecture, code and quality, security, data, operations, documentation and service expectations. The outcome is one of four: accepted as it is, accepted with conditions and a transition backlog, assessment or rescue needed before service starts, or declined where responsible support is not possible.
Formal service transition

Operations are not an informal extension of a project. Before service-level-backed operation begins we agree service boundaries, support contacts, escalation, monitoring, runbooks, access, maintenance responsibilities, known exceptions and any initial remediation.
Improvement, not ticket handling

Each service keeps an improvement backlog covering reliability, automation, cost, security, user friction and product evolution. AI appears here as monitoring, incident response, evaluation, cost and quality optimisation and continuous improvement of live AI.

title: AI Transformation
summary: AI pressure exists, but value, governance, data and the path to production are unclear. Turn AI ambition into operational value.
problemStatement: Organisations face pressure to adopt AI, but value depends on choosing the right use cases, having data that is ready, governing the risk, integrating with real workflows and running reliably in production. Leadership wants measurable results without a safe, prioritised route from experimentation to production.
signals: AI pilots are scattered across teams and few have reached production.
The return on AI investment is unclear.
Important workflows are still manual even where AI could help.
The data AI would need is fragmented or of uncertain quality.
Nobody is sure what governance, privacy and human oversight AI use requires.
Prototypes that impressed in a demonstration stall before production.
impact: Without a prioritised route, AI effort spreads across disconnected experiments that never reach live use. Data, security and governance gaps surface late, and operational cost, reliability and dependence on a single vendor are discovered only after commitments have been made.

children.text: Successful AI transformation needs more than a model. It needs a value strategy, data readiness, product and engineering work, Responsible AI, change and adoption, and managed operation once the capability is live.
One team across practices

Consulting identifies and prioritises opportunities and builds the business case. AI & Data designs, evaluates and governs the capability. Engineering integrates and secures it in production. Managed Services operates, evaluates and improves it. Experience joins where the interface matters. You work with one accountable engagement lead throughout.
Principles we hold to
Every use case needs a business or user outcome.
Evaluation criteria are defined before production launch.
Bounded, measurable workflows come before broad autonomous systems.
Data readiness, security, privacy and human oversight are explicit decisions.

phases.title: Assess
phases.description: Identify where AI could create value, and the readiness gaps in data, process, controls and skills.

phases.title: Prioritise
phases.description: Rank opportunities by value, feasibility, data readiness and risk, and choose the use case worth testing.

phases.title: Prototype
phases.description: Test the strongest business and technical hypothesis quickly, against evaluation criteria agreed in advance.

phases.title: Production
phases.description: Engineer a secure, integrated and observable capability, with human oversight and fallback behaviour designed in.

phases.title: Scale
phases.description: Extend the capability across workflows, teams, systems or business units where further adoption creates value.

phases.title: Operate
phases.description: Monitor, evaluate, optimise and govern the live capability, reviewing value, quality and risk continuously.

faq.question: Do we have to start with an assessment?
faq.answer: Not always. Where data or readiness is uncertain, an AI Opportunity Assessment is the responsible start, because it tests feasibility, quality and risk before you commit to production. If the use case is already clear and the data is understood, we can move to a prototype.

faq.question: Will a successful prototype go straight into production?
faq.answer: No. Prototype evidence does not automatically mean production readiness. Production AI needs evaluation, monitoring, security and human-oversight decisions appropriate to the use case, and prototype work does not include production hardening unless that is agreed.

faq.question: Are you tied to one AI model provider?
faq.answer: No. We stay pragmatic about technology and vendors, and we make operational cost, reliability and provider dependence part of the design rather than an afterthought.

faq.question: How are model, API and cloud usage costs handled?
faq.answer: Usage costs are kept visible: they are separated from professional fees or capped by agreement, so a technically successful system does not become an unexpected cost.

faq.question: Will you be able to tell us where our data goes?
faq.answer: That is the aim: Vitalos should be able to answer which model or provider processes your data, whether it is used for provider training, where it is stored, what retention applies, what tools and permissions an agent has, how outputs are evaluated and what happens when the model fails.

title: Business Process Modernisation
summary: Manual, fragmented or inefficient operations constrain growth and service. Redesign the work, then automate and integrate it.
problemStatement: Manual, slow or fragmented workflows create cost, delay and risk. When critical processes depend on spreadsheets, re-keying, email chains and disconnected tools, operations limit growth and service quality instead of supporting them.
signals: Critical processes depend on spreadsheets, manual re-keying or email chains.
The same information is entered into several systems by hand.
Handoffs between teams or systems cause delays and errors.
Leaders cannot see how work is flowing until it is too late to act.
Growing volume means adding people to the same manual steps.
impact: Fragmented operations add cost and delay to every transaction, introduce errors at each manual handoff and make service quality depend on individual effort. They also hide the operational data leaders need to improve the business.

children.text: We start from the process, not the technology: map how the work happens today, redesign it, then use software, integration, automation and AI where each helps. Analytics show whether the change worked.
One team across practices

Consulting leads process discovery and redesign. Engineering builds and integrates the systems. AI & Data adds intelligent automation and operational intelligence. Experience makes the new workflow usable for the people who run it.
Automation that stays reliable

Deterministic workflow automation, systems integration and AI are combined deliberately. Integrations are validated for failure modes, retries and dependence on external systems before they carry live work.

phases.title: Discover
phases.description: Map the current process, the people and systems involved, the pain points and the measures that matter.

phases.title: Redesign the process
phases.description: Define the target workflow before choosing technology, removing steps rather than automating them.

phases.title: Automate and integrate
phases.description: Build the software, integrations and automation the redesigned workflow needs, with AI where it adds value.

phases.title: Measure
phases.description: Compare the live process against its baseline using agreed operational measures.

phases.title: Improve
phases.description: Extend automation to adjacent processes and keep refining the workflow as the business changes.

faq.question: Is this just buying automation software?
faq.answer: No. The work starts with how the process should run. Software, integration and automation follow the redesign, so the result is a better workflow rather than a faster version of the old one.

faq.question: Do you replace our existing systems?
faq.answer: Only where replacement is the right answer. Often the bigger gain comes from connecting the platforms you already have so information flows automatically between them.

faq.question: Where does AI fit?
faq.answer: AI is combined with deterministic workflow automation and software integration where it creates measurable value. Bounded, measurable workflows come first.

faq.question: Who owns the process after go-live?
faq.answer: Ownership after the engagement is made explicit before it ends. Your team can take over with documented handover, or Vitalos can continue to operate and improve the workflow under a defined service.

seo.title: Business Process Modernisation
seo.description: Redesign manual, fragmented operations, then automate and integrate them so the business can grow.

title: Digital Product Transformation
summary: A new or existing digital product must create measurable value for customers or employees. Discover, design, engineer, launch and improve it.
problemStatement: The organisation needs a new platform, portal, application, commerce experience or digital service, or an existing one that works much better. The product has to create measurable value for customers or employees, not just ship features.
signals: A new digital proposition is planned but its users, journeys and scope are not yet validated.
An existing product has weak adoption or a poor experience.
Customer or employee journeys are fragmented across tools.
The product cannot change quickly enough to keep up with the business.
Previous build attempts stalled or became hard to maintain.
impact: Building before the problem and users are understood wastes engineering investment. Products that are hard to use are not adopted, and products that cannot evolve after launch stagnate.

children.text: Experience leads discovery and design, Engineering builds for production, and Consulting keeps the product tied to the business outcome. Discovery, design and engineering run as one engagement rather than separate handoffs.
From discovery to continuous improvement

Product discovery validates the problem, users, journeys and scope before major build. Engineering then delivers working increments with testing, security and accessibility checks, and the product keeps improving after launch.

phases.title: Discover
phases.description: Validate the problem, users, journeys and scope, and set the direction for a prototype and delivery backlog.

phases.title: Design
phases.description: Design the service, journeys and interface, and the technical architecture, ready for build.

phases.title: Engineer
phases.description: Build in working, tested increments through controlled environments, with peer review and automated checks.

phases.title: Launch
phases.description: Validate the release for function, security, performance and accessibility, then move to production with rollback planned.

phases.title: Improve
phases.description: Review outcomes against measures and keep evolving the product through continuous improvement.

faq.question: Can we go straight to build?
faq.answer: Yes, when the product objective is clear, requirements are understood well enough, constraints are known, decision-makers are available and dependencies are understood. Otherwise a short product discovery is the safer start.

faq.question: Do you build brochure websites?
faq.answer: Vitalos builds web platforms, portals, commerce and digital products. Routine brochure websites are generally not part of what we offer.

faq.question: What happens after launch?
faq.answer: You can take over with documented handover, or keep Vitalos engaged for continuous product improvement against an agreed roadmap.

faq.question: Is accessibility included?
faq.answer: Yes. Interfaces are checked against the accessibility target agreed for the engagement as part of validation before release.

title: Application Modernisation
summary: Legacy applications create cost, risk, slowness or integration limits. Modernise in controlled stages towards a platform you can keep changing.
problemStatement: Ageing applications and architecture constrain growth, reliability and the speed of change. They are expensive to maintain, risky to alter and hard to integrate with the rest of the business.
signals: Small changes to a core application take a long time or carry unusual risk.
Only a few people understand how the system works.
Integration with newer platforms is difficult or impossible.
Reliability, security patching or hosting are becoming a concern.
Maintenance absorbs budget that should fund improvement.
impact: Legacy constraints slow every initiative that depends on the system, increase operational and security risk, and make the organisation dependent on knowledge held by a few people.

children.text: Modernisation starts with an honest assessment of architecture, dependencies and migration constraints. From there we agree a target architecture and modernise, replace or progressively refactor in controlled stages, so the business keeps running while the system changes.
One team across practices
Consulting leads assessment and target architecture. Engineering migrates and refactors. Managed Services takes over operation through a formal transition, so the modernised system does not stagnate.

phases.title: Assess
phases.description: Establish the architecture, technical debt, dependencies, risks and migration constraints of the current system.

phases.title: Target architecture

faq.question: Do we have to replace everything at once?
faq.answer: No. Modernisation can replace, re-platform or progressively refactor parts of the system in stages, chosen by risk and value.

faq.question: Why start with an assessment?
faq.answer: Material legacy complexity is one of the cases where going straight to build is risky. An assessment establishes the architecture, dependencies and migration constraints first.

faq.question: Who supports the system during and after modernisation?
faq.answer: Responsibility is explicit at every stage. After transition, your team can take over with documented handover or Vitalos can operate it under Application Care.

faq.question: Can you modernise a system another supplier built?

title: Data & Intelligence Transformation
summary: Data is fragmented, unreliable or not turning into decisions and AI capability. Build the foundation, then the intelligence on top of it.
problemStatement: Data exists across several systems but is fragmented, low-confidence or difficult to turn into decisions. Management lacks reliable operational intelligence, and the data is not ready to support AI.
signals: Different reports give different answers to the same question.
Producing management information involves manual spreadsheet work.
Data sits in several systems with no agreed definitions or ownership.
AI initiatives stall because the data they need is not ready.
impact: Decisions are made on figures nobody fully trusts, analysts spend their time reconciling data instead of using it, and AI initiatives cannot move beyond experiments.

children.text: We connect, clean, model and govern the data first, then build reporting, decision systems and AI on a foundation that can be trusted.
Controls that keep data trustworthy
Source ownership and lineage.
Data quality expectations and monitoring for pipeline failure and freshness.
Schema and contract management.
Access control, minimisation, and retention and deletion rules.
Documented business definitions for the metrics that matter.
One team across practices
AI & Data leads the data and intelligence work, Consulting ties it to the decisions the business needs to make, and Engineering integrates the source systems.

phases.description: Map data sources, quality, ownership and the decisions the data should support.

faq.question: Do we need a new data platform?
faq.answer: Not necessarily. The assessment shows whether connecting and governing existing sources is enough, or whether a new platform is justified.

faq.question: Is this preparation for AI?
faq.answer: Often. AI adoption depends on data foundations, governance and systems integration. Good reporting is valuable in its own right, and it is also the base that later AI work builds on.

faq.question: How do you handle data quality and ownership?
faq.answer: Each important source gets an owner, lineage and quality expectations, and key metrics get documented definitions, so reports can be traced back to their data.

faq.question: Where does AI come in?
faq.answer: Once the foundation can be trusted, advanced analytics or AI can be built on it, under the same evaluation, monitoring and governance controls as any other production AI.

title: Technology Recovery & Reliability
summary: A critical platform is unstable, slow or unfinished. Triage it, establish a known baseline, stabilise and remediate, then operate it.
problemStatement: A critical platform is unstable, slow or unfinished. It may have been built by another supplier, documentation may be thin, and the business depends on it working.
signals: Incidents and outages are frequent or hard to diagnose.
A project has stalled and the product is unfinished.
Performance is degrading as use grows.
The original supplier or team is no longer available.
Nobody can say with confidence what is safe to change.
impact: An unstable critical platform disrupts operations and customers, consumes the people who keep it running and blocks every improvement that depends on it.

children.text: Recovery starts with triage and an assessment that creates a known technical baseline. Stabilisation and controlled remediation follow, in priority order, before Vitalos accepts ongoing operational responsibility.
Honest about outcomes

Before accepting a service commitment for an inherited system, we assess ownership and access, architecture, code, security, data, operations and documentation. If the risk, access or legality make responsible support impossible, we say so.

phases.title: Triage
phases.description: Understand the immediate risk and protect what the business depends on today.

phases.title: Assess
phases.description: Establish a known baseline: architecture, code quality, security posture, operations and documentation.

phases.title: Stabilise
phases.description: Address the causes of instability that matter most, in priority order.

phases.title: Remediate
phases.description: Work through a prioritised recovery plan, with each change reviewed, tested and reversible.

phases.title: Operate
phases.description: Move into managed engineering or application care with a defined service boundary.

faq.question: Will you take over a system another supplier built?
faq.answer: Yes, after an assessment. Acceptance is never automatic: we need to understand architecture, code ownership, dependencies, security, deployment, data responsibilities, known incidents and documentation first.

faq.question: Can you guarantee the system will be fixed?
faq.answer: We do not promise outcomes before the assessment. It establishes what is wrong and what recovery involves, and it can conclude that a rescue is needed before any service starts, or that responsible support is not possible.

faq.question: What if the right answer is to rebuild?
faq.answer: Then the assessment says so. Recovery, modernisation and replacement are all legitimate outcomes, chosen on evidence.

faq.question: What happens once the system is stable?
faq.answer: It moves into managed engineering or application care within a defined service boundary, or back to your own team with documented handover.

title: AI opportunity and readiness assessment framework
summary: A concept for a reusable framework that ranks AI use cases by value, feasibility, data readiness and risk, so assessments reach consistent recommendations.
is: A defined concept for an assessment framework: the questions, criteria and outputs an AI Opportunity Assessment works through, written down so that each assessment is consistent and comparable.
isNot: Not software, not a scoring product and not a substitute for the judgement of the engagement team.
limitations: This page describes a concept drafted from Vitalos's own delivery methods. It makes no claim about any implementation, results or client use; none are published here. The criteria have not been independently reviewed, weightings and thresholds are not defined, and the framework would need evidence from real assessments before it could be treated as an accelerator.

children.text: The question
How can an organisation choose between AI ideas on evidence, rather than on enthusiasm or the latest demonstration?
What the framework would assess
Value: the business or user outcome, and what happens if nothing changes.
Feasibility: whether the workflow, systems and integration make the use case buildable.
Data readiness: whether the data the use case needs exists, is accessible and is of known quality.
Risk: security, privacy, human oversight and the consequences of the model being wrong.
Organisational readiness: governance gaps, ownership and the capacity to adopt the change.
What it would produce
An opportunity map and ranked use cases.
A feasibility and risk view for each.
A recommendation on which use case, if any, is worth a prototype.
Principles it would encode

No AI for its own sake; bounded, measurable workflows before broad autonomous systems; evaluation criteria defined before production; operational cost, reliability and vendor dependence understood early.

seo.title: AI opportunity and readiness framework (concept)
seo.description: A concept for ranking AI use cases by value, feasibility, data readiness and risk. Concept maturity: no implementation is claimed.

title: Production AI evaluation harness
summary: A concept for repeatable testing of AI models and agents against agreed quality and risk criteria, before release and whenever a model, prompt or data source changes.
is: A concept for a reusable evaluation approach: representative test cases and agreed criteria that an AI capability is measured against before release and re-measured when anything material changes.
isNot: Not a product, not a benchmark and not evidence that any particular AI system is safe or effective.
limitations: This page describes a concept drafted from Vitalos's own delivery methods. It makes no claim about any implementation, results or client use; none are published here. No test suites, datasets or results exist on this page, and how it would integrate with specific model providers has not been designed.

children.text: The question
How do you know an AI capability is good enough for live use, and that it is still good enough after the model, prompt or data changes?
What the harness would check
Task success against a clearly defined metric.
Behaviour on representative test cases, including difficult and harmful inputs.
Grounding and retrieval quality where the system uses retrieval.
Failure and fallback behaviour, and when a person is brought in.
Cost and latency against agreed budgets.
Regression when the model, provider, prompt or data source changes.
Why it matters
Prototype evidence does not automatically mean production readiness. Repeatable evaluation turns that judgement into evidence, and keeps it current as models and context change.

limitations: This page describes a concept drafted from Vitalos's own delivery methods. It makes no claim about any implementation, results or client use; none are published here. The checklist depth, evidence standards and how findings convert into a transition backlog are not yet defined.

children.text: The question
When is it responsible to accept a service commitment for a system you did not build?
Assessment domains
Ownership and access: code, infrastructure, accounts, domains, data, licences and administrative control.
Architecture: services, dependencies, integrations, hosting and critical failure points.
Code and quality: maintainability, tests, build process, known defects and technical debt.
Security: authentication, access control, secrets, vulnerabilities, patching and incident history.
Data: stores, backups, retention, privacy responsibilities and recovery expectations.
Operations: deployments, monitoring, logs, alerts, incidents and release ownership.
Documentation: runbooks, architecture records and business-critical knowledge.
Service expectations: hours, criticality, planned changes and escalation routes.
Possible outcomes
Accepted as it is.
Accepted with conditions and a transition or remediation backlog.
Assessment or engineering rescue required before service begins.
Declined, where risk, access, legality, a capability gap or the commercial model make responsible support impossible.

seo.title: Inherited-system takeover assessment (concept)
seo.description: A concept for assessing a system built by others before accepting operational responsibility. Concept maturity: no implementation is claimed.

title: Security
summary: Security is designed into how we work and what we deliver, not added at release.

children.text: This page sets out the standards Vitalos works to and is putting in place. They are commitments, not certified controls.
In our own operations
Vitalos is putting in place a minimum security foundation for its own systems:
multi-factor authentication and least-privilege access on critical systems, with periodic access reviews;
managed credentials and secrets, which are never committed to source control;
timely security updates, and vulnerability and dependency management;
a documented security incident response procedure;
joiner, mover and leaver access processes, including for contractors;
an inventory of suppliers and of the third parties that process data for us.
In the systems we deliver
Our delivery standard is:
security and privacy by design, proportionate to exposure, data, business criticality and regulatory context;
version control, peer review and automated checks before material changes reach production;
a security gate before release, reviewing attack surface, identity, secrets and dependency risks;
contractors and partners working to Vitalos security standards, with access removed promptly when no longer needed.
Reporting a security concern
Security contact: [Monitored security contact, to be confirmed by the owner].

title: Privacy
summary: Personal data should be collected only when it is needed, and handled deliberately.

children.text: This page sets out the standards Vitalos works to and is putting in place. They are commitments, not certified controls.
On this website
Enquiry forms collect only what is needed to respond to and qualify an enquiry.
Enquirers are not subscribed to marketing.
Our standard is to keep personal data out of general platform logs.
In client delivery
Our standard is that:
where delivery involves personal data, its purposes, collection, access, retention, third-party processing and deletion are made visible;
whether Vitalos acts as controller or processor is assessed, with a data processing agreement where Vitalos processes data on a client's behalf;
higher-risk processing goes through a data protection impact assessment;
legal interpretation is escalated to qualified advisers, because engineering judgement does not replace legal advice.
The website privacy notice sets out how personal data is handled through this site.

seo.description: The data protection standards Vitalos works to on this website and in client delivery.

title: Responsible AI
summary: AI must solve a legitimate problem, stay accountable to a person and be evaluated before and after it goes live.

children.text: Principles
Purpose: AI must solve a legitimate business or user problem.
Accountability: a human owner remains responsible for every deployed system.
Transparency: clients understand material model and provider limitations and where AI is used.
Privacy and security: sensitive data is handled deliberately and access is controlled.
Evaluation: production AI is tested against defined quality and risk criteria.
Human oversight: higher-risk decisions include appropriate review or escalation.
Fairness: foreseeable discriminatory or harmful outcomes are considered.
Reliability: failure, fallback and provider or model change are designed for.
Traceability: important instructions, models, data sources and evaluations are versioned where appropriate.
Continuous monitoring: material AI services are re-evaluated as models, prompts, data and context change.
Questions we aim to answer

For an AI system we deliver, Vitalos aims to be able to answer where your data goes, which model or provider processes it, whether it is used for provider training, where it is stored, what retention applies, what tools and permissions an agent has, how outputs are evaluated and what happens when the model fails.

seo.description: The Responsible AI principles Vitalos applies to the AI systems it designs, builds and operates.

draftProvenance.omitted: Stage 6 §9 says Vitalos should publish simple principles early; the procurement answers are worded as an aim ("should be able to answer") for the owner to confirm.

title: Accessibility
summary: This website is being built to WCAG 2.2 Level AA, and the services we deliver are checked against an agreed accessibility target.

children.text: This website

The target for this website is WCAG 2.2 Level AA, treated as a build requirement rather than an after-launch audit: semantic structure, keyboard operation, visible focus, sufficient contrast, accessible forms, reduced-motion support and reflow without loss of function.
A full accessibility statement will be published after the site has been evaluated. We do not display conformance badges without a supporting assessment.
Services we deliver
Our delivery standard makes accessibility one of the quality gates before release: applicable interfaces are checked against the accessibility standard agreed for the engagement.

draftProvenance.omitted: No conformance claim or accessibility statement: the site has not been evaluated yet (Stage 8 §24).

title: Resilience
summary: Recovery should be planned and tested in proportion to how critical a service is.

children.text: This page sets out the standards Vitalos works to and is putting in place. They are commitments, not certified controls.
Our standard is that:
recovery requirements match data and service criticality: what can be restored, from where, how long it should take and who decides;
a backup that has never been validated is not treated as proven recovery capability;
every production release has a rollback or recovery plan, and a deadline is not approval to skip it;
incidents are classified by severity, with immediate escalation and recovery first for critical events;
live services have explicit ownership, monitoring and runbooks before service-level-backed operation begins.
Specific response targets belong in each service agreement; they are not promised generically here.
